11.2.new:
after this write that is untrue for a refused item; the line was not changed.
    - ASK 607, A GATE CHANGE IN NO LINE FORM THE ENGINE READS DOES NOT REMOVE THE SEAT (md_notes_rulings 546; one Shared Library line, both copies, in sbApply2024; the gate prompt is not changed).
      1. The refusal push "the CHANGE TO line has no line form the engine reads" carries the tag rfs:'pkgFRM' after "lines:[o]". It is the fourth push with a tag (item 1 of ASK 549 above names the other three).
      2. The reader is the one of ASK 549, item 2 above; it is not changed. When the judge answered CHANGE to a NOT APPLIED gate item and the change has no line form the engine reads, the item stays not cured, its reason reads "pkgFRM refused the gate change; the judge's line before the change stands (recorded, no seat removed): <the refusal's reason>", and it is stored with live:false: RECORD-ONLY, adding 0 to drv_uncured. This holds in Gate Record, Alt Gate Record and R2 Alt Gate Record.
      3. The judge's line before the change stands in the judgment. That is so also when the change was the judge withdrawing its own line (a CHANGE TO of "NONE"): the withdrawn line stays in the judgment text.
      4. Unchanged: a silent item is still UNCURED and counted; a KEEP answer and an applied change give the same rows as before; a change refused because "the flagged line is not in the judge text" carries no tag and is still counted; at the send-back stage the tag is carried on the item and not read. The reader stands in the NOT APPLIED branch only, so a form refusal on a gate item of another kind would still be counted; the stored record holds none (25 counted form refusals, all on NOT APPLIED items).
      5. Shown offline: on stored judgment 1122 (judge luna; enforcer log rows 29285 to 29295, a CHANGE TO of "NONE" on eleven NOT APPLIED items) eleven counted items become none counted. Not shown by a run; a gate form refusal is rare. Mark: an E-GATE row whose reason begins "pkgFRM refused the gate change" and which is RECORD-ONLY, with the seat not removed for it.
    - ASK 561, THE DEFENDER'S OPENING

- GEMINI 4 HYDROGEN AND GEMINI 4 NEON DEBATE AND JUDGE (ASK 623; engine: Init Seats, Resolve Seats, Build Synthesis, Build Independent Verdict, Build Diagnostic Prompt; database: one `model_config` row, `dash_debaters`, `odv1_record_panel_substitution`, `dash_judge_lineup`, `dash_odv1_debates`, `dash_odv1_judges` and the table `odv1_judge_order`; where it differs from any entry above in this section, this rule is right):
  - Seats: `hydrogen` (`google/gemini-4-hydrogen`) and `neon` (`google/gemini-4-neon`), both of family google, each read from the `model_config` row of its own name. The neon row is new (provider openrouter, role engine, active). The hydrogen row is the row the alternate already read; it is not changed. The inactive row `gemini_deb` is not read.
  - Debaters: Init Seats `ENG` holds hydrogen and neon, each reading the seat of its own name, so either can be named as defender or challenger. `dash_debaters` lists both, so the launch page offers them and `dash_launch_odv1` accepts them. The engine accepts 12 debaters (deepseek stands in `ENG` and is refused by name, §3), which is 132 pairings.
  - Judges: `FAM_PANEL` holds neon as google, and the call-family maps (`JFAM_I` in Init Seats; `JFAM` in Resolve Seats, Build Synthesis, Build Independent Verdict and Build Diagnostic Prompt) hold neon as openrouter, as they hold hydrogen. Both seats stand in the table `odv1_judge_order` at the end of the alternate list. Either sits on the panel only when the operator moves it there on the Judge order page and saves. As alternates they can be offered a removed judge's seat with no save, after the alternates ahead of them in the list.
  - The rules of this section bind both seats as they bind every seat: a Google debater keeps gemini, hydrogen, neon and argon off the seat list; no judge runs a debater's model; the enforcer is never of a debater's family. With neon against hydrogen, either way, no Google seat judges and the enforcer is luna.
  - NO EFFORT SETTING: no request to hydrogen or neon carries a reasoning field, on any call, debater or judge; each runs at the provider's default (§4, NO REASONING FIELD).
  - Recorders and page: the seat list of `odv1_record_panel_substitution` holds neon (it already held hydrogen). `odv1_record_panel_alternates` admits both seats by its own rule and refuses a Google alternate when a Google model debates. `dash_judge_lineup` holds neon in its family table and its call-family table; `dash_odv1_debates` and `dash_odv1_judges` hold neon in the judge sort list.
  - Pairs with no seat behind the panel, under the judge order as saved: twelve. Chatgpt or sol62 against gemini, hydrogen or neon, either way, seats spark, qwen4max and sonnet, with the backup enforcer, and has no reserve and no alternate.
  - Shown offline: Init Seats and Resolve Seats on the 132 pairings: 128 seat three judges and 4 stop with the line of THE ENFORCER IS NEVER OF A DEBATER'S FAMILY (chatgpt or sol62 against glm, either way), as before. On the 90 earlier pairings the panel, the reserve and the enforcer are what they were; only the end of the alternate list differs. `dash_judge_lineup` equals the engine on the 128. One check call to each model, with a stored round-1 defender request and no reasoning field, returned a whole answer with finish reason stop; most of each answer's output tokens were reasoning (hydrogen 10,870 of 14,453; neon 11,922 of 16,582).
  - Limits: not shown by a run in any role. Neither seat has debated under its own name, and the engine has never called neon in any role. The limits of hydrogen as a judge stand (ALTERNATE HYDROGEN in this section; §17). Marks: a `debate_results` row that names hydrogen or neon as defender or challenger, with every round and a judgment; a JUDGE ORDER line that seats one of them and a `debate_judgments` row from it.
